repo_standards_ref: docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md, docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md, references/global-crew.md; existing utilization package (g1/g2/g3) + src/physics numpy conventions; #628 batch-script convention

smells.finding: compose_and_persist_weekend (~145 lines) and positive_control (~90 lines) are long. Both are cohesive, sectioned, and linear (per-constructor ceiling loop, then per-driver g3 loop; control construction + jitter sweep), so this is a NON-BLOCKING observation: the per-driver g3 row-build loop could be extracted for readability. Subordinate to the repo's batch-script idiom (#628 collect-style orchestration).

The ceiling->simulate_lap->np.interp v_ideal build appears in both compose_and_persist_weekend and _run_validation (rebuilt so the jackknife scores the SAME fixed profile). NON-BLOCKING observation: a small _constructor_v_ideal(inputs, constructor) helper would remove the ~4-line repeat. Deliberate for coherence, not a defect.

override.repo_standard: The (year, session_type, gp_name, round_idx/map_version) identity tuple is the established store-key convention threaded through the whole epic-659 utilization package (class_ledger g1, reference_lap_product g2, reference_utilization_store, class_utilization_observable g3 all pass it positionally/by-keyword).
override.reason: Introducing a bespoke identity object here would diverge from the sibling modules' signatures the CLI composes, breaking match-the-surrounding-code (global-crew implementation discipline); the clump is the package's shared key, not an accidental grouping.

override.repo_standard: src/physics represents lap profiles as raw numpy arrays (distance_m/v_ideal/v_real) and class identities as bare strings (SegmentMap.class_ids), the pervasive convention across segment_map + utilization modules.
override.reason: Wrapping distances/speeds/class-ids in value objects would fight the numeric package idiom and the SegmentMap interface the module consumes; primitives here are the domain's established vocabulary, not under-modelling.

smells.finding: load_weekend_inputs takes ~11 keyword-only params (three are data-source paths: telemetry_store, grip_bin_db, per_year_db_path). NON-BLOCKING observation: the data-source paths could be grouped into a small paths object. Mitigated by keyword-only + defaults, and mirrors the derivation modules' explicit-seam signatures.
